_note: v2 hook overrides for la Rue Commerçante (B07_rue_commercante). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs (no text or numbers, no weapons).

fr_epicerie_noun.hook: "ay-PEA-suh-REE": at the GROCER'S the grocer tips A PEA out of her scoop: "SORRY!"

fr_shopping_noun.hook: The PENGUIN ("shoh-PING") goes SHOPPING with bags dangling from both flippers.

fr_copie_noun.hook: "koh-PEA": the parrot squawks "COPY!" and types out a perfect COPY of the letter.

fr_bourg_noun.hook: A model MARKET TOWN of red-roofed toy houses, so quiet it is a BORE ("BOOR").
fr_bourg_noun.why: The painting shows the model houses only; no fountain or yawning boy.

fr_rabais_noun.hook: The RABBIT ("ra-BAY") snips the price in half with his scissors: a big DISCOUNT on carrots.
fr_rabais_noun.why: No price tag is painted; the rabbit holds the scissors.

fr_abonne_noun.hook: The lady in A BONNET ("a-bo-NAY") comes back every week: the carrot merchant's most loyal SUBSCRIBER.
fr_abonne_noun.why: The painting shows a lady in a bonnet beside the merchant, no ducklings.

fr_troc_noun.hook: A BARTER at the TRUCK ("TROK"): the little goat is swapped for the toy truck full of cabbages.
fr_troc_noun.why: The goat stands beside a toy truck of cabbages; no farmers.

fr_negociant_noun.hook: The MERCHANT ("nay-go-SYAHN") holds out his armful of carrots and haggles over the price: a seasoned MERCHANT.
fr_negociant_noun.why: The merchant sells carrots rather than cloth.

fr_libraire_noun.hook: "lee-BRAIR": two young BOOKSELLERS in caps and aprons hand a book across the crate.
fr_libraire_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_caissier_noun.hook: "kay-SYAY": KAY the CASHIER rings up a sale at her till by the back window.
fr_caissier_noun.why: No rabbit is painted; she stands at the till.

fr_passant_noun.hook: A PASSER-BY in a long coat tips his hat as he strolls along the back wall, just PASSING ("pah-SAHN") through.
fr_passant_noun.why: He walks along the back wall, not in the doorway.

fr_vendeur_noun.hook: "vahn-DUR": the balloon SELLER holds up his bunch of balloons: a true VENDOR.
fr_vendeur_noun.why: He stands in the middle of the room, not by the door.

fr_enchere_noun.hook: The woman beside the CHAIR ("ahn-SHAIR") waves her paddle high to make a BID.
fr_enchere_noun.why: She stands beside the chair rather than on it.

fr_halle_noun.hook: "Welcome to my MARKET HALL!": Uncle AL ("AL") spreads his arms while a boy peeks out of the window behind him.
fr_halle_noun.why: The boy peeks from a window.

fr_reduction_noun.hook: The DUCK ("ray-DEWK-syohn") waddles proudly across the shop floor: everything is at a REDUCTION today, a DUCK-count!

fr_carnet_noun.hook: "kar-NAY": the toy pony rears up with a "NAY!" beside the little red toy CAR: CAR + NAY = un carnet, a NOTEBOOK.
fr_carnet_noun.why: The pony and the toy car are painted; the notebook is in the sound.

fr_edition_noun.hook: "ay-dee-SYOHN": the old gentleman settles on his stool with a first EDITION and his tea cup on A DISH.
fr_edition_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_floral_adj.hook: Two bumblebees buzz nearby, sure the lady in the FLORAL ("flo-RAHL") dress is a flower bed.
fr_floral_adj.why: The bees hover above the flowers next to her.

fr_palette_noun.hook: Being a good PAL, the old painter LETS ("pa-LET") the kitten dab its paws on her PALETTE.
fr_palette_noun.why: The painter is an old woman.

fr_materiau_noun.hook: "MAT, TERRY, OH!" ("mah-tay-RYOH"): Terry in his flat cap sits on his stack of planks: building MATERIAL.
fr_materiau_noun.why: Terry sits on the planks; there is no doormat.

fr_espace_noun_f.hook: Like English 'space', said ehs-PAHS: the apprentice calls "S, PASS!" and passes a blank metal SPACE block to the old typesetter, who presses it into the gap between two words in his tray of type.
fr_espace_noun_f.why: relocated from ciel (typographic space); painted in the print shop

fr_broche_noun.hook: Like English 'brooch', said BROSH, like 'brush': a grand old lady BRUSHES the big sparkling purple BROOCH pinned to her shawl until it gleams.
fr_broche_noun.why: relocated from foret birds (brooch belongs at the jeweller); painted at the window

fr_commercant_noun.hook: "ko-mair-SAHN": the cheerful SHOPKEEPER with the big moustache sweeps his shop floor.
fr_commercant_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_depot_noun.hook: "day-POH": little PO in his blue cap sweeps out the toy bus DEPOT.
fr_depot_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_sabot_noun.hook: "sa-BOH": the little girl with a red BOW in her hair clatters about in wooden CLOGS.
fr_sabot_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_adherent_noun.hook: The boy proudly wears his club badge: he is a MEMBER. "A DAY I RAN ("ah-day-RAHN") the meeting!"
fr_adherent_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_manuel_noun.hook: "ma-NWEL": the boy reads a MANUAL on building a bookshelf and shrugs: "Oh WELL…"
fr_manuel_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_livre_noun_m.hook: "LEEVR": "LEAVE your BOOK here," says the girl on top, adding one more BOOK to her wobbly tower.
fr_livre_noun_m.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_vogue_noun.hook: The latest VOGUE ("VOG"): two models in sunglasses strut down the purple rug like a catwalk.
fr_vogue_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_icone_noun.hook: The tall fashion ICON ("ee-KOHN") poses in a pointy CONE party hat.
fr_icone_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_jade_noun.hook: The lady in a silk robe slips a smooth green JADE ("ZHAD") bangle onto her wrist.
fr_jade_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_glamour_noun.hook: The lady in pearls and a spotted gown strikes a GLAMOUR pose, dreaming of the MOOR ("gla-MOOR").
fr_glamour_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_correspondant_noun.hook: "CORRESPOND ON!" ("ko-res-pohn-DAHN"): the boy on the floor reads the latest letter from his PEN PAL among piles of stamps.
fr_correspondant_noun.why: Repainted: the animal acting human is now a person (LESSONS 2); hook follows the painting.

fr_racheter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe BUYS BACK his fluffy grey toy RAT from the toy chest: RAT-SH-TAY (rash-TAY).
fr_racheter_verb.why: RAT + acheter → racheter = to buy back, to buy more (racheter un jouet). RED beret = regular -er.

fr_revendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe RE-SELLS his old bicycle at the auction to the man in the cap: RE-VENDOR (ruh-VAHN-dr).
fr_revendre_verb.why: RE-VENDOR → revendre = to resell, to sell on (revendre son vélo). PURPLE beret = regular -re.

fr_debattre_verb.hook: With a painted moustache, Monsieur Verbe DEBATES the price of the lot, finger raised (day-BAH-tr).
fr_debattre_verb.why: DEBATE → débattre = to debate, to discuss (débattre du prix). GOLD beret = irregular. (like battre)

fr_stand_noun.hook: Like English 'stand', said STAHND: a little wooden flower STAND, a market stall with a red-and-white striped awning, its counter full of flower bunches.
fr_stand_noun.why: RECS p11 plan move (montagne/pentes snowmen stand removed); ventes is full, so painted in the florist's courtyard (market street).

fr_colporteur_noun.hook: "kol-por-TUHR" sounds like COAL PORTER: a sooty-faced pedlar bent under a basket heaped with a sack of coal trudges from stall to stall, selling his coal door to door: a PEDLAR.
fr_colporteur_noun.why: RECS p12 plan move (route raccoon removed); human pedlar on the right as requested; ventes is full, so painted in the florist's courtyard.
